Operator-based epoch de-mixing and gain-corrected trial regression across lags

Source: R/diagnose_crossrun_recovery.R
decon_epoch_regression.Rd

Estimate trial-by-trial correlations and regression slopes across epoch lags relative to a target event while removing preceding/neighboring event leakage, correcting regularization-induced amplitude attenuation, and propagating per-trial operator precision weights and within-run error covariance.

Usage

decon_epoch_regression(
  deconvolution,
  covariates = NULL,
  events = NULL,
  target_condition = NULL,
  lags = seq(-2, 4, by = 1),
  readout_kernel = c("triangle", "linear", "boxcar", "gaussian"),
  readout_width = NULL,
  demix_other_events = TRUE,
  demix_target_trials = TRUE,
  demix_within_trial = FALSE,
  demix_ridge = 0.05,
  within_trial_ridge = 0.06,
  gain_floor = 0.05,
  restore_scale = FALSE,
  source_model = c("impulse", "window", "duration"),
  trial_durations = NULL,
  duration_scale = c("rate", "integral"),
  weighting = c("precision", "gls", "none"),
  tau2_mode = c("auto", "residual", "marginal"),
  aggregate_by_parcel = FALSE,
  parcel_groups = NULL,
  whiten_panel = FALSE,
  return_epochs = FALSE,
  return_panel = FALSE
)

Arguments

deconvolution

Result of deconvolve_crossrun_hrf().

covariates

Optional numeric vector, matrix, or data.frame of trial-level predictors for target trials (concatenated across runs or supplied as a run-named list matching deconvolution$hrf_fit$run_ids). When NULL (default), performs covariate-agnostic epoch readout, de-mixing, biological variance estimation (tau2_mode = "marginal"), Empirical-Bayes precision weighting, and optional within-run ZCA whitening (whiten_panel = TRUE), returning the trial panel (return_panel defaults to TRUE when covariates = NULL) for downstream two-stage mixed_by behavioral modeling or inter-region connectivity (R2 ~ R1_seed * x).

events

Optional run-named list of event data.frames with onset and optional condition and duration. Defaults to the HRF fit's event tables.

target_condition

Optional character scalar naming the target event condition in events[[r]]$condition (e.g., "feedback"). When supplied, non-target events in events[[r]] are treated as interfering events whose leakage into the target epoch is removed when demix_other_events = TRUE.

lags

Numeric vector of epoch readout lags (in seconds) relative to each target event onset.

readout_kernel

Epoch readout kernel: "linear", "boxcar", "triangle", or "gaussian". Default: "triangle".

readout_width

Optional kernel full width in seconds for non-linear readouts (defaults to 1.5 * tr).

demix_other_events

Logical; whether to estimate non-target event contributions at their own onsets and subtract their operator-predicted leakage into each target epoch lag. When demix_ridge >= 0.03 (default 0.05), uses a condition-mean non-target de-mixing operator that removes preceding cue/event bleed without inflating target-trial variance; when demix_ridge < 0.03 (e.g. 0.02), activates a 2nd-order iterated Tikhonov joint \((T, O)\) operator to de-mix strongly trial-varying non-target confounds. Default: TRUE.

demix_target_trials

Logical; whether to use the stratum resolution matrix at each lag to de-mix adjacent target-trial overlap and restore regularization-attenuated amplitude gain via 2nd-order iterated Tikhonov inversion (solve_duration_demix_operator()). Default: TRUE.

demix_within_trial

Logical; whether to apply an additional multi-lag point-spread de-mixing step across the requested lags (when at least 3 lags are evaluated) to sharpen temporal localization across lags within each target trial. Recommended (TRUE) when estimating within-trial temporal waveforms \(\beta(\tau)\) across a multi-lag grid. Default: FALSE.

demix_ridge

Positive ridge stabilization parameter for target and non-target cross-talk inversion. Values >= 0.03 (default 0.05) use condition-mean non-target de-mixing; values < 0.03 activate joint trial-varying non-target de-mixing. Default: 0.05.

within_trial_ridge

Positive ridge stabilization parameter for multi-lag within-trial point-spread inversion when demix_within_trial = TRUE. Default: 0.06.

gain_floor

Minimum absolute operator gain used when correcting amplitude slopes. Default: 0.05.

restore_scale

Logical; if TRUE, multiplies each run and voxel by its recorded deconvolution$scaling[[r]]$scale divisor so that beta_raw and beta_corrected (and panel readouts) are reported in unscaled physical input units rather than standardized (zscore/noise_sd) units. Strongly recommended (TRUE) when pooling across multiple runs in mixed_by. Default: FALSE.

source_model

Forward neural source model at each target lag: "impulse" (default unit impulse at onset + lag), "window" (local sustained boxcar of width readout_width centered at onset + lag), or "duration" (trial-varying sustained boxcar over [onset + lag, onset + lag + d_i] using each target trial's duration d_i from trial_durations or events[[r]]$duration, with duration-matched readout and unpenalized baseline-rate de-confounding).

trial_durations

Optional numeric vector (concatenated across runs) or run-named list of non-negative target trial durations (in seconds), such as per-trial reaction times. Overrides events[[r]]$duration for target trials and defaults source_model to "duration" when source_model is not explicitly specified.

duration_scale

Scaling convention for positive-duration target trials when source_model = "duration": "rate" (default; trial amplitude represents neural firing rate / boxcar height per TR bin, so integrated neural activity scales with duration and constant baseline firing rates are de-confounded from duration variability) or "integral" (each trial boxcar is normalized to unit time-integrated neural mass across its duration).

weighting

Trial regression weighting scheme across target trials and runs: "precision" (default; Empirical-Bayes / floor-stabilized inverse error-variance weights propagating per-trial operator standard errors and run noise scale), "gls" (null-mode-damped, Bartlett-adaptive within-run ZCA correlation whitening plus precision weighting accounting for off-diagonal trial-to-trial error correlations), or "none" (unweighted OLS). All three slope estimates (beta_unweighted, beta_weighted, beta_gls) and their standard errors are always included in coefficients.

tau2_mode

Estimator for biological trial-to-trial variance \(\hat{\tau}^2_{\mathrm{bio}}\) used in Empirical-Bayes trial precision weights and within-run ZCA whitening: "auto" (default; uses "marginal" when covariates = NULL and an Empirical-Bayes blend of residual and marginal estimators when covariates are supplied), "residual" (method-of-moments estimator from OLS covariate regression residuals minus projected operator variance \(\mathrm{tr}((\mathbf{I}-\mathbf{P}_X)\boldsymbol{\Omega})\)), or "marginal" (covariate-agnostic estimator combining run-centered marginal variance, lag-1 trial difference variance, and robust MAD scale minus analytical operator variance expectations).

aggregate_by_parcel

Logical; if TRUE, aggregates deconvolved signals across voxels within each spatial parcel (using inverse-variance voxel precision weights and empirical spatial noise correlation propagation) prior to Stage-2 epoch de-mixing and Stage-3 regression/ZCA whitening. Replaces voxel-by-voxel Stage-3/4 fitting with parcel-level inference while calibrating se_demixed, tau2_bio, precision_weight, and ZCA whitening directly on the high-SNR parcel series. Default: FALSE.

parcel_groups

Optional character or factor vector of parcel/region labels for each voxel (either unnamed of length n_voxels or named by voxel_ids). Defaults to deconvolution$hrf_fit$specification$spatial_groups when aggregate_by_parcel = TRUE. Supplying a non-NULL parcel_groups automatically enables aggregate_by_parcel = TRUE.

whiten_panel

Logical; if TRUE and return_panel = TRUE, adds within-run null-mode-damped, Bartlett-adaptive ZCA-whitened outcome (decon_demixed_whitened) and covariate (<var>_whitened) columns to panel so downstream mixed_by(..., weights = "precision_weight") models account for both heteroscedastic trial precision and off-diagonal within-run trial error correlations. Recommended (TRUE) for group mixed-effects inference. Default: FALSE.

return_epochs

Logical; whether to include raw and de-mixed trial-by-voxel (or trial-by-parcel) epoch matrices per lag. Default: FALSE.

return_panel

Logical; whether to return a tidy MEDUSA-compatible data.table (panel) with columns run, trial, event_index, onset, evt_time, voxel (and parcel when aggregate_by_parcel = TRUE), decon_raw, decon_demixed, se_raw, se_demixed, precision_weight, precision_weight_op, precision_weight_raw, error_ac1, tau2_bio, and the covariate columns for downstream mixed_by() modeling. Defaults to TRUE when covariates = NULL and return_epochs = FALSE.

Value

A list with coefficients (per voxel/parcel, lag, and predictor term), summary (averaged across usable units per lag and term), optional epochs, optional panel, and settings.

Details

decon_epoch_regression() bridges continuous regularized deconvolution and trial-level cognitive neuroscience models in five stages:

  1. Kernel Quadrature Readout: At each requested lag \(\tau\), continuous deconvolved activity is integrated around each target event using readout_kernel. For source_model = "duration", the readout window centers on the trial's midpoint \(t_i + \tau + 0.5 d_i\) and expands to \(\max(w_{\mathrm{src}}, d_i)\).

  2. Non-Target Event De-Mixing (demix_other_events): Using the frozen inverse operator \(\mathbf{D}_r\) and forward HRF design \(\mathbf{G}_{r,0}\), the function subtracts resolution-predicted leakage from non-target events (e.g., cues or motor responses) using a condition-mean operator (demix_ridge >= 0.03) or a 2nd-order Tikhonov joint \((T, O)\) operator (demix_ridge < 0.03).

  3. Target Cross-Talk & Duration De-Mixing (demix_target_trials): Inverts the lag-specific target resolution matrix via a 2nd-order iterated Tikhonov operator (solve_duration_demix_operator()) with per-trial effective gain restoration to remove trial-to-trial overlap and divide out regularization-induced amplitude shrinkage. In source_model = "duration", a centered-subspace penalty and rank-1 baseline adjustment keep constant baseline firing rates invariant to trial duration (preventing reaction-time confounding).

  4. Optional Multi-Lag Point-Spread De-Mixing (demix_within_trial): When enabled across \(\ge 3\) lags, sharpens temporal specificity across lags using a 2nd-order Tikhonov lag-by-lag resolution inverse while preserving cross-trial operator covariance structure.

  5. Analytical Uncertainty, Precision Weights & Null-Mode-Damped ZCA Whitening: Propagates observation-level AR(1) noise covariance through the composite linear readout/de-mixing operator \(\mathbf{B}_{r,\tau}\) to obtain exact per-trial standard errors (se_demixed), adjacent-trial error autocorrelation (error_ac1), Empirical-Bayes precision weights (precision_weight), covariance-propagated sandwich SEs (se_weighted), and null-mode-damped, Bartlett-adaptive within-run ZCA-whitened variables for mixed_by.

Recommended Best-Practice Configuration

Across the 5-pillar MEDuSA Monte Carlo validation suite (amplitude recovery, temporal alignment, inter-region connectivity, factorial power surfaces, and biophysical Windkessel-Balloon + fmrisim scanner realism), the recommended end-to-end configuration is:

  1. Stage 0–1 (HRF Estimation): Use hrf_library(tr, preset = "medusa") (pruned 3D physiological manifold spanning fast/narrow/minimal-undershoot subcortical through slow cortical HRFs with positive-lobe normalization; ~44 candidates, or preset = "canonical_27" for the 27-candidate fixed-undershoot canonical grid) and estimate_crossrun_hrf with noise_model = "ar1", evidence = "calibrated", selection_mode = "soft_average" (evidence-weighted HRF kernel averaging across locally supported shapes), and parcel labels in spatial_groups.

  2. Stage 2 (Deconvolution): Use deconvolve_crossrun_hrf with lambda = NULL (adaptive prewhitened GCV tuning), scaling = "noise_sd" (AR(1) innovation noise SD rather than total "zscore" variance), and penalty = "sobolev".

  3. Stage 3 (Epoch De-Mixing, Parcel Pre-Aggregation & Whitening): Use decon_epoch_regression(..., demix_other_events = TRUE, demix_target_trials = TRUE, restore_scale = TRUE, weighting = "gls", aggregate_by_parcel = TRUE, whiten_panel = TRUE, return_panel = TRUE). Enable demix_within_trial = TRUE with lags spaced at \(1\times\mathrm{TR}\) when estimating multi-lag waveforms \(\beta(\tau)\) (if lags is sampled finer than \(1\times\mathrm{TR}\), within_trial_ridge is automatically scaled by \((\mathrm{TR}/\Delta\tau)^2\) to prevent sub-TR collinearity amplification), and set source_model = "duration" (duration_scale = "rate") when modeling variable-duration (RT) epochs.

  4. Stage 4 (Group Mixed-Effects Inference): Pass both the ZCA-whitened panel columns and precision weights to mixed_by: mixed_by(panel, decon_demixed_whitened ~ x_whitened + (1 + x_whitened | id), weights = "precision_weight").
